title: Opportunistic Screening for Atrial Fibrillation With Continuous ECG Monitoring in the Emergency Department
summary: In a retrospective cohort of 65,244 consecutive adults receiving continuous ECG monitoring in one academic ED, 1,945 (3.0%) were discharged with at least 30 seconds of previously undocumented AF and no documented anticoagulation. Of these, 1,385 (71.2%) met the study's CHA2DS2-VASc criteria for anticoagulation. Undiagnosed AF was associated with 2.6 ischemic strokes per 100 person-years and an adjusted stroke HR of 3.00 (95% CI 2.39-3.76) versus patients without AF.
findings: 1,945/65,244 (3.0%) were discharged with undiagnosed monitor-detected AF.
1,385/1,945 (71.2%) met the study's CHA2DS2-VASc anticoagulation criteria.
Ischemic stroke incidence was 2.6 per 100 person-years in the undiagnosed-AF group.
Adjusted stroke HR was 3.00 (95% CI 2.39-3.76) versus no AF and 1.32 (95% CI 1.02-1.71) versus known AF.
comparator: Patients with no AF on monitoring and patients with already known AF for stroke-risk analyses.
population: 65,244 unique consecutive adults who received continuous ECG monitoring in an academic emergency department from 2020 through 2024.
shortTitle: Continuous ECG finds undiagnosed AF in the ED
limitations: Retrospective, single-center, selected population limited to patients placed on continuous monitoring; AF detection and downstream treatment were not randomized. A 30-second episode may not carry uniform treatment implications, and residual confounding affects the stroke association.
intervention: Opportunistic retrospective identification of at least 30 seconds of atrial fibrillation on continuous ED ECG monitoring.
whyItMatters: ED monitor data may contain clinically relevant AF that is never converted into a diagnosis or follow-up plan. Systems that capture and review sustained AF episodes before discharge could improve recognition, but this observational study does not show that automatic screening or anticoagulation from brief monitor episodes improves outcomes.
evidenceNotes: Primary PubMed abstract reviewed; PMID 40650644, DOI 10.1016/j.annemergmed.2025.06.008, Epub July 12, 2025. Later correspondence emphasized interpretation limits related to the presenting diagnosis, reinforcing the observational nature of the finding. Targeted correction search found no verified correction.
primaryEndpoint: Proportion discharged with monitor-detected AF without documented AF diagnosis or anticoagulation.
